title: Naval Communications Nomenclature Matching Test
description: Drag and match the official military alphanumeric nomenclature on the left with its corresponding equipment name and operational function on the right.

pairs.definition: The legacy Automated Digital Network System (ADNS) router currently being retired from the fleet.
The modern Automated Digital Network System (ADNS) variant installed Afloat to coordinate and route shipboard IP enclaves.
The modern Automated Digital Network System (ADNS) variant installed at Shore sites (NCTAMS/NCTS) to terminate fleet data paths.
A bright red voice-switching cabinet used to electrically connect crypto units to shipboard red phones.
An electronic switch capable of routing both digital and analog interfaces and creating tactical voice conference calls.
The standard physical patch panel (RED indicating unsecure/decrypted data, BLACK indicating encrypted data).
The satellite RF modem manufactured by Comtech EF Data used on ships for digital data circuits.
A multiplexer that combines four individual incoming signals at 16 kbps on UHF satellite circuits.
A demultiplexer used to split composite signal feeds specifically for the Fleet Satellite Broadcast.
An upgraded cryptographic hardware device used to secure tactical UHF/VHF voice radio communications.
A handheld fill device used to store and load Cryptographic Keying Material (KEYMAT) into equipment.
The phased-array radar on cruisers and destroyers that handles searching, tracking, and missile guidance simultaneously.
A massive, floating, mobile radar station designed to track ballistic missiles under heavy weather and sea conditions.
